LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.headline: Cole Kmet suffered ‘likely season-ending injury' during Bears-Patriots game: Reports
away.blurb: Chicago Bears’ star tight end Cole Kmet is believed to have suffered a serious and potentially season-ending knee injury on a fourth-quarter reception against the New England Patriots Thursday night at Soldier Field, according to reports. NFL Network and ESPN reporter Ian Rapoport said Kmet was undergoing testing Friday morning. “Until those results come back, there is no finality,” Rapoport wrote in a post on X. Kmet had caught a pass on second down from quarterback Caleb Williams with 5:34 left to go in the game, and was moving toward the first-down marker when he was hit by two Patriots defenders. Kmet immediately began grabbing his right knee on the sideline, and was tended to by trainers for the Bears. After the TV timeout, Kmet was seen being carted off the field, giving a thumbs up to Bears fans as he left the field. The game ended in a 30-24 Bears victory . When asked at Kmet’s injury status following the game, Coach Ben Johnson didn’t sound optimistic. “We’ll know more tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good,” he said. Kmet has been a key reserve player for the Bears this season, serving as a mentor to Colston Loveland and still playing significant snaps for Chicago during the season. If Kmet misses any time, rookie Sam Roush would likely see more action on offense. Johnson was expected to address the media at 1 p.m. Friday. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. Bears are 2nd-best team in the NFC when healthy Contact/Follow @TrojansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of USC Trojans news, notes and opinion. The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh Forces Two Turnovers The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league. At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11. The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5). New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to. Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one. The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game . Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week. Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team. The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2. That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers. After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

Pittsburgh Steelers veteran safety DeShon Elliott was trending in the right direction at practice throughout the week. The team took the last step for Elliott to make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the New Orleans Saints . On Saturday, the Steelers announced they have activated Elliott from the reserve/injured list. He will be eligible to play Sunday against the Saints in the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Paris, France. Elliott fully practiced Wednesday and Thursday before the team flew to Europe. The Steelers then canceled their Friday practice in France. The veteran safety doesn't have a designation on the team's injury report. Barring a last-minute setback, Elliott will dress for the first time this season versus the Saints. On Wednesday, the Steelers released safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The team didn't make a corresponding move, which left open a roster spot for Elliott on Saturday. Elliott started this season on the PUP list because of a knee injury he sustained last season. Elliott hyperextended his knee, which required surgery, in Week 8 almost exactly a year ago on October 26. In five games during 2025, Elliott posted 38 combined tackles. He also had one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits, one sack, two pass defenses and one interception. Elliott began his career in the AFC North with the Baltimore Ravens . He spent three seasons with the Ravens, where he became a regular starter in 2020. Pittsburgh Steelers veteran safety DeShon Elliott was trending in the right direction at practice throughout the week. The team took the last step for Elliott to make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the New Orleans Saints . On Saturday, the Steelers announced they have activated Elliott from the reserve/injured list. He will be eligible to play Sunday against the Saints in the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Paris, France. Elliott fully practiced Wednesday and Thursday before the team flew to Europe. The Steelers then canceled their Friday practice in France. The veteran safety doesn't have a designation on the team's injury report. Barring a last-minute setback, Elliott will dress for the first time this season versus the Saints. On Wednesday, the Steelers released safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The team didn't make a corresponding move, which left open a roster spot for Elliott on Saturday. Elliott started this season on the PUP list because of a knee injury he sustained last season. Elliott hyperextended his knee, which required surgery, in Week 8 almost exactly a year ago on October 26. In five games during 2025, Elliott posted 38 combined tackles. He also had one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits, one sack, two pass defenses and one interception. Elliott began his career in the AFC North with the Baltimore Ravens . He spent three seasons with the Ravens, where he became a regular starter in 2020. picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. Brock Purdy has been incredible and is currently the betting favorite for MVP, but you have to look at the massive schedule assistance this team has received. The 49ers opened the year against a jet-lagged Rams team in Australia, followed by a string of home games against broken offenses like the Broncos and Dolphins . San Francisco's only true road test was a highly fluky win in Seattle. Now, the injury bug is biting them. The 49ers are likely going to be without Nick Bosa and Kyle Juszczyk, but the biggest blow is Mike Evans ., who suffered an Achilles injury on Monday Night Football. The offensive splits for San Francisco with and without Evans are night and day. The veteran averages an elite 0.33 EPA per route run — the highest in the Next Gen Stats era — and serves as Purdy's ultimate safety valve over the middle of the field on critical third downs. Additionally, there is a fascinating historical trend here: Purdy is just 3-6 against the spread (ATS) when playing in a domed stadium. You simply cannot overcome that kind of variance. Offensively, Michael Penix Jr. changes the entire dynamic of this team. If the Falcons can stay on script and avoid falling behind early, they have the ultimate weapon in Bijan Robinson to relentlessly attack a 49ers defense that is suddenly missing Dre Greenlaw and struggling to stop the run. 49ers vs Falcons Spread Pick to Make This is the ultimate "amateur psychologist" spot. I expect Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson to exploit San Francisco's injuries, control the clock, and keep this game highly competitive. Fade the overpriced 49ers here. home.headline: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson, LB Divine Deablo ruled out vs. 49ers
home.blurb: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson, LB Divine Deablo ruled out vs. 49ers Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Atlanta has several key players who are questionable for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. That includes the Atlanta Falcons and San Francisco 49ers, who each enter Sunday's game with availability questions for key players. Atlanta's injury report has been lengthy all week long, but it includes a few players who could be making a return in Week 7. Most notably are cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson. Their return would bolster a secondary that has been dinged up in recent weeks but was playing well at the start of the season. If Terrell, who has been on injured reserve for the last four games, and Henderson do return, that could afford a bit of flexibility in the secondary, especially with slot cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. ruled out for Sunday due to a hamstring injury he sustained late in Week 6. Bowman is one of four players ruled out against the 49ers. The others are linebacker Divine Deablo, offensive tackle Michael Jerrell and running back Brian Robinson Jr., the latter two of whom first appeared on Wednesday's injury report as limited participants with bicep and hamstring injuries, respectively. Deablo has been the key communicator for Atlanta's defense this season, but the team feels confident that rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable for the game with a neck injury , can step up in that area if needed. The Falcons had three players begin practicing this week after spending time on injured reserve. While those three players—wide receiver Beaux Collins, offensive lineman Cameron Williams and Terrell—are listed as questionable for the game, they would need to be added to Atlanta's active roster by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to play on Sunday. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston (12) scores on a touchdown reception during the fourth quarter against New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens (21) at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published Oct 21, 2026 LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. picks.blurb: Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans: Week 7 Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Week 7 updates Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans: Week 7 Predictions Spencer German Sat, October 24, 2026 at 1:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads At 4-2 and in first place in the AFC North, the Cleveland Browns are starting to really earn some respect across the NFL, but a loss to the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 would erase some of that good will they've built up in recent weeks. Aside from their records, these two teams are oddly similar. Their defenses tend to carry them and keep games close, while their offenses tend to struggle, particularly early on in games. Cleveland is well-equipped to win those slog-style games, but will they slip up in the Music City? Here are our predictions for Week 7. Anthony Moeglin It's a Cleveland Browns party on Broadway this weekend in Nashville, Tennessee. The Browns come into this game as the favorite for the first time all season and probably the last time all season. They have a chance to get to 5-2 on the year and stay in first place. They get it done on Sunday against the Titans. Spencer German Last week was a barometer game to assess how the Browns stack up with a legitimate Super Bowl contender, even if that contender was missing it's MVP quarterback. But this week, in some ways is an even bigger test of whether or not the Browns are as good as their record says they are. Great teams beat the teams they're supposed to beat and Cleveland does just that on Sunday to improve to 5-2. Yes, it is basically a Pick 'Em heading into Sunday. Cleveland is -1.5 favorites in this one, and I see a 20-3 winner for Cleveland where the defense shuts it down, and the offense gets it going a little bit on Sunday. This one is basically a Pick 'em with the Browns being listed as favorites for the first time this season (and on the road nonetheless) by 1.5. I think that means they easily cover, with a 17-9 victory. A 300-yard day for Deshaun Watson I'm 0-6 on bold predictions this year, so let's go way out there. Deshaun Watson throws for 300 yards on Sunday for the first time in his Cleveland Browns career. It would be a monumental day down in Tennessee if this bold prediction comes true. The Browns score 7 on their opening drive Despite Todd Monken's presence as an elite offensive mind, the Browns have yet to score on an opening drive this season. They've also only scored six points in the first quarter this season. In a game featuring two struggling offenses, the one that gets off to a better start could be in the driver's seat for a win. Finally, Cleveland gets to play with a lead.

picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Week 7 updates Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. It seems like every week a big favorite is being upset, and Week 6 had two of them as the Los Angeles Rams (12.5-point favorites) lost outright at home to the Arizona Cardinals while the Indianapolis Colts (seven-point favorites) lost an AFC South battle with the previously winless Tennessee Titans. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. Kyler Murray should be able to produce enough offense to let his defense lead them to a win in this interconference duel. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. However, they do not match up well with the Minnesota Vikings this Sunday. The Indianapolis Colts (2-4) will attempt to ground themselves on Sunday as they travel to Minneapolis to face the host Minnesota Vikings (5-0) before their season truly spirals out of control. The Colts' 2026 campaign is at a crossroads. After consecutive losses, including an embarrassing finish last week to the previously winless Tennessee Titans , the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard . Will that move spark the Colts and help them turn the tide, or will the team retreat into its shell? Trade rumors and thoughts of a slide are once again surrounding the Colts. This game could be a back-breaker unless they can avoid it. Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Vikings 23, Colts 13 "I'd often like to lead with the optimistic take on the matchup with a clear advantage the Colts have over their opponent, but I'm not sure there is one this week. Minnesota's defense blitzes far more than any other team, which is something the Colts' offense struggles against. The Colts can usually run the ball, but opponents are running against Minnesota less than anyone else because of the defensive fronts the Vikings present. The Vikings' offense isn't doing well despite having Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson, but they've had a week to figure out what to do, coming off their bye. "The Colts would often have the edge on special teams and penalties, but Minnesota's special teams are just as good as Indy's, if not better, and the Colts and Vikings are tied for being the second-least-penalized teams in the NFL. No Tyler Warren or Sauce Gardner for the Colts, and Minnesota doesn't have a soul on the injury report. The Vikings have the clear advantages in this one." Jake on the season: 2-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Vikings 19, Colts 9 "The Colts limp into Minnesota coming off of their most embarrassing loss since 2024. They are without two of their best players in Warren and Gardner, while the 5-0 Vikings are looking healthy coming out of their bye week. "The Vikings boast the top defense in football, while the Colts' offense can't get out of their own way. This seems to be a recipe for disaster, with very little room for the Colts to make up this disadvantage. This should be an ugly kickers duel, with the Vikings coming out on top." Zach on the season: 4-2 The Colts take on the Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS .

Kyler Murray's injury update and matchup against the Colts That weakness could give Murray more time to read the field and allow receivers to find space downfield. away.headline: Vikings can make the Colts pay now that Christian Darrisaw is back
away.blurb: Christian Darrisaw’s return from concussion protocol invites the Minnesota Vikings to attack downfield against Indianapolis this afternoon. The Week 7 injury report has him available, and Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner is out with a calf injury. Indianapolis has pressured quarterbacks on just 24.4 percent of dropbacks through six games, the NFL’s lowest rate, according to Next Gen Stats figures in the Vikings’ official preview. The Colts also allow 27.3 points per game. Kevin O’Connell should make Indianapolis defend the entire field. O’Connell should get a little more ambitious with Darrisaw back. Better protection on Murray’s left can create room for longer play fakes and deeper throws, putting more pressure on a secondary already missing Gardner. The Vikings have the receivers to stretch this defense. This is a good week to let them. How Christian Darrisaw can expand the Minnesota Vikings’ passing game Longer-developing play action requires protection through the fake, Murray’s reset, and the receivers’ breaks. If Darrisaw handles his edge assignment without help, O’Connell has more freedom to release a tight end or back immediately instead of assigning a chip that delays his route. A Jordan Addison post paired with a Justin Jefferson deep crosser is one appealing option. Addison can carry a safety deep while Jefferson crosses behind the linebackers. Murray needs a pocket long enough to see which defender commits and throw accordingly. Addison and T.J. Hockenson are returning, too. Hockenson can threaten the seam or provide an intermediate outlet if Indianapolis keeps its safeties deep. Gardner’s absence reduces the Colts’ coverage options, but it doesn’t guarantee Jefferson single coverage. Murray already completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards against New Orleans . He has only two touchdown passes across his three full starts this season. Adding deeper combinations would force defenders to respect more than the throws Minnesota can complete before the rush arrives. Interior protection remains a concern. Donovan Jackson’s season-ending knee injury leaves Minnesota vulnerable at left guard, where DeForest Buckner could disrupt those longer plays. Darrisaw can win his matchup and still watch Murray get hurried. O’Connell needs answers inside, too. Trusting Darrisaw alone could allow Minnesota to direct more blocking help toward Buckner, preserving space for Murray to step forward as the deeper routes develop. Third-and-long will test a different skill set than early-down play action. When the Colts can ignore the run fake, Murray needs room to climb the pocket and find a receiver beyond the sticks without scrambling to keep the drive alive. Getty Just one day after releasing running back DeeJay Dallas, the Minnesota Vikings brought back the veteran. He will play in Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the NFL transaction wire, the Vikings signed Dallas to their practice squad Saturday. The team then elevated him to the active roster for the Week 7 matchup versus the Colts. home.headline: Murray Set To Play: QB expected to start vs Colts; Vikings urged to attack downfield
home.source: The Times of India on MSN
home.blurb: Running back Jordan Mason presents a different situation. He is preparing to return from injured reserve but remains questionable with a thumb injury. His status could affect Minnesota's plans in the running game and influence how the Vikings distribute their offensive workload. Note: This update reflects the supplied report dated October 24, 2026. Confirm the official inactive list before kickoff, as the available information does not independently verify Murray's final game status. Kyler Murray faces a key test as the Minnesota Vikings prepare to take on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. The quarterback could have a valuable opportunity to exploit a struggling pass rush, but Minnesota must make the right decisions to turn that advantage into points. The latest injury report offers encouraging news for the Vikings' receiving group, giving Murray potential options at every level of the field. However, the bigger question is whether Minnesota can move away from its reliance on short screen passes and make the most of the time its quarterback may have in the pocket. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Will Kyler Murray play against the Indianapolis Colts today? Minnesota also received positive news about its key offensive weapons. Wide receiver Justin Jefferson, tight end T.J. Hockenson and wide receiver Jordan Addison all practised in full and carry no game designation, according to the report. Their availability could give Murray more options as he looks to challenge Indianapolis through the air. Kyler Murray's injury update and matchup against the Colts That weakness could give Murray more time to read the field and allow receivers to find space downfield. Jefferson and Addison offer options for deeper throws, while Hockenson can provide a target over the middle. However, Indianapolis can still make life difficult for the Vikings. The Colts often use eight defenders in coverage, limiting open passing lanes and encouraging quarterbacks to throw underneath. Minnesota must recognise when a short pass makes sense and when a more aggressive option offers greater value. The Vikings' heavy use of screen passes has become a concern because the approach has not consistently produced efficient results. Against a defence that struggles to generate pressure, Murray and head coach Kevin O'Connell have a chance to change that pattern. The key will be balance. Murray does not need to force risky throws, but Minnesota cannot afford to waste the extra time its offensive line may provide. If the Vikings mix quick passes with intermediate routes and well-timed deep attempts, they could make the Colts pay for their defensive weaknesses. home.headline: Vikings can make the Colts pay now that Christian Darrisaw is back
home.blurb: Christian Darrisaw’s return from concussion protocol invites the Minnesota Vikings to attack downfield against Indianapolis this afternoon. The Week 7 injury report has him available, and Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner is out with a calf injury. Indianapolis has pressured quarterbacks on just 24.4 percent of dropbacks through six games, the NFL’s lowest rate, according to Next Gen Stats figures in the Vikings’ official preview. The Colts also allow 27.3 points per game. Kevin O’Connell should make Indianapolis defend the entire field. O’Connell should get a little more ambitious with Darrisaw back. Better protection on Murray’s left can create room for longer play fakes and deeper throws, putting more pressure on a secondary already missing Gardner. The Vikings have the receivers to stretch this defense. This is a good week to let them. How Christian Darrisaw can expand the Minnesota Vikings’ passing game Longer-developing play action requires protection through the fake, Murray’s reset, and the receivers’ breaks. If Darrisaw handles his edge assignment without help, O’Connell has more freedom to release a tight end or back immediately instead of assigning a chip that delays his route. A Jordan Addison post paired with a Justin Jefferson deep crosser is one appealing option. Addison can carry a safety deep while Jefferson crosses behind the linebackers. Murray needs a pocket long enough to see which defender commits and throw accordingly. Addison and T.J. Hockenson are returning, too. Hockenson can threaten the seam or provide an intermediate outlet if Indianapolis keeps its safeties deep. Gardner’s absence reduces the Colts’ coverage options, but it doesn’t guarantee Jefferson single coverage. Murray already completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards against New Orleans . He has only two touchdown passes across his three full starts this season. Adding deeper combinations would force defenders to respect more than the throws Minnesota can complete before the rush arrives. Interior protection remains a concern. Donovan Jackson’s season-ending knee injury leaves Minnesota vulnerable at left guard, where DeForest Buckner could disrupt those longer plays. Darrisaw can win his matchup and still watch Murray get hurried. O’Connell needs answers inside, too. Trusting Darrisaw alone could allow Minnesota to direct more blocking help toward Buckner, preserving space for Murray to step forward as the deeper routes develop. Third-and-long will test a different skill set than early-down play action. When the Colts can ignore the run fake, Murray needs room to climb the pocket and find a receiver beyond the sticks without scrambling to keep the drive alive. home.headline: Vikings Make U-Turn With Running Back Before Colts Game
home.blurb: With Mason back, the Vikings will have a full complement of running backs available against the Colts. Mason will serve as an RB2 and perhaps even split carries with veteran starter Aaron Jones Sr. Vikings Make U-Turn With Running Back Before Colts Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Brewers' stunning comeback Vikings Make U-Turn With Running Back Before Colts Game Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings brought back running back DeeJay Dallas on the practice squad and elevated him for the Week 7 matchup versus the Indianapolis Colts. Getty Dave Holcomb Sun, October 25, 2026 at 2:40 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Running back DeeJay Dallas will play for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Getty Just one day after releasing running back DeeJay Dallas, the Minnesota Vikings brought back the veteran. He will play in Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the NFL transaction wire, the Vikings signed Dallas to their practice squad Saturday. The team then elevated him to the active roster for the Week 7 matchup versus the Colts. The Vikings also announced the round of transactions with Dallas. Minnesota released Dallas from the active roster Friday to create space on the active roster for fellow running back Jordan Mason. On Saturday, the Vikings also activated Mason from injured reserve to the roster. Both running backs will play against the Colts. "To make room for Mason, the Vikings released running back DeeJay Dallas," wrote Vikings.com's Craig Peters . "Minnesota then signed Dallas to its practice squad. The veteran first joined Minnesota's practice squad in September and was signed to the 53-man roster after Mason's injury." To have space for Dallas on the practice squad, Minnesota released cornerback Natrone Brooks . Vikings Bring Back DeeJay Dallas, Elevate RB to Active Roster for Week 7 GettyRunning back DeeJay Dallas will play for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Mason left in Week 1 with a fractured thumb. Needing surgery, he landed on injured reserve and missed the next four games. Week 7 was the earliest he could come off IR. In his first season with the Vikings last year, Mason had 758 rushing yards with six touchdowns. He had 59 yards and a score before leaving against the Green Bay Packers in the season opener. In his absence, Jones has carried the Vikings backfield with 410 rushing yards and two scores. He's also caught 12 passes for an additional 72 yards. Dallas only had three rushing attempts with Mason not in the lineup. He played every week but lined up for only 40 offensive snaps while receiving 92 snaps on special teams. Against the Colts, Dallas will provide extra depth behind Jones and Mason while likely focusing on special teams. The Vikings could also have rookie Demond Claiborne active for the matchup. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. The offense is stagnant, generating a meager 14.0 points per game, ranking 31st in the NFL. The passing game led by Malik Willis has been particularly painful to watch. Miami has managed just two passing touchdowns to four interceptions on the year. You simply cannot win football games in the modern NFL with a passing attack that completely lacks explosion and turns the ball over at that rate. The Dolphins are averaging just 5.1 yards per play and converting a dismal 29.8% of their drives into scores. The defense hasn't offered much resistance either. Miami is giving up 26.4 points per game and allowing opponents to score on 50% of drives. Opposing quarterbacks are torching this Dolphins secondary, racking up 11 passing touchdowns to just three interceptions, while averaging an explosive 7.4 net yards per attempt. The defense looks gassed, spending far too much time on the field due to the offense's inability to sustain drives. New York hasn't exactly set the world on fire either. New York is making opponents work for every yard, holding opposing offenses to a mere 38.1% scoring rate on drives and forcing turnovers on 11.1% of opponent possessions. away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.blurb: News Sports Restaurants Real Estate Opinion Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals MIAMI DOLPHINS Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win Joe Schad Palm Beach Post Updated Oct. 23, 2026, 12:24 p.m. ET The winless Miami Dolphins are looking to reset after a bye week and secure their first victory against the New York Jets. Coach Jeff Hafley hopes to get his first NFL head-coaching win in his home state of New Jersey. Players have identified key areas for improvement, including reducing turnovers and penalties. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. Wasn't a friendly first five weeks of the season. It was tough, kind of going through that. And we still got to live with it, but I think that break gives you a chance to kind of reflect and kind of take a deep breath and I think that's what this team needed." Predictably, the Dolphins' statistical resume after five games is poor. Miami ranks better than the league average in only 8 of the top 32 essential categories sorted and ranked by the NFL. What have the Dolphins done fairly well? "Right now, we're a team that's running the ball very well, and we're playing pretty good run defense, too," Hafley said. "We're a physical team. I think we have to build on that identity and continue to grow and develop." Miami Dolphins seek development, but also a win A lot of growth, development and patience will be required. Coaches often say they use the bye week to "self-scout" in an attempt to improve in areas they may have overlooked in the day-to-day grind of a game week. "With such a small sample size, it's not huge, but a really good time to evaluate and catch your breath and sometimes when you get to step back, you can see some things clearly," Hafley said. There are many areas in which the Dolphins must improve to win a game (short-term goal) and finish better than, say, 2-15 or 3-14 this season. But here are some self-scout reflections Dolphins players have spoken about after the bye. home.headline: Dolphins’ Caleb Douglas cleared to return from ankle injury against Jets
home.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Florida & Caribbean Experiences Florida Jewish Journal Florida Jewish Journal Branded Content Paid Partner Content MIAMI GARDENS — Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas is cleared to play in the upcoming game against the New York Jets on Sunday. Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. The 6-foot-4 target who led the team with 94 receiving yards in the team’s opener against the Las Vegas Raiders could provide a boost to the passing game. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. CBS Sports analyst Pete Prisco has not once picked the Panthers to win, and they've proved him wrong thrice. This time, though, he's going with the surging Panthers, although he's still not predicting a big performance. Prisco picked a one-point Panthers win, saying, "The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around." His CBS colleague John Breech is also picking the Panthers, but he's taking them by a field goal. Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff is picking a Panthers win, 24-16, betting on the Bryce Young-led offense to continue clicking at home. SI's Ian MacMillan isn't buying any of what the Panthers are doing, and he's picking the Buccaneers to upset them in Charlotte. "Time to sell high on [the Panthers]. Their offense has been phenomenal to start the year, but I have plenty of questions surrounding the ability of some of the defenses they've had to face... I wouldn't be surprised to see them significantly regress. It could start this weekend when they take on a Tampa Bay defense that's fourth in opponent EPA per play and eighth in opponent success rate," he wrote. Here's how the rest of the SI staff is predicting this one: Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers John Pluym: Panthers Matt Verderame: Panthers Peter Dewey: Panthers Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer disagrees, predicting a 24-17 win. "Jalon Daniels is doing his best to keep the Bucs' competitive with help from the running game. The defense is also bringing a good pass rush of late. away.blurb: And he couldn't have picked a better time to be reportedly making his return. The Bucs are just 1-5, but a win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon would thrust them right back into the mix in an always wide-open division. It won't be easy, but having their franchise QB back — along with a rapidly improving defense — should go a long way. Mayfield still has a questionable tag, but that's really just a formality at this point. The former No. 1 overall pick logged full practices on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, after which head coach Todd Bowles confirmed that Mayfield would be returning to the lineup in Week 7. How limited he might be remains to be seen, but the fact that he was able to put in a full week of practice is undoubtedly a good sign. We also have to wait and see whether there are any signs of rust; Mayfield has been out since suffering a thumb injury in a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, nearly a full month of action. That said, while he was up and down before getting hurt — completing 63.5 percent of his passes but for just 6.4 yards per attempt with two touchdowns and two picks — it's hard not to feel like he raises the ceiling of a Bucs offense that desperately needs a spark. Fantasy football ramifications of Baker Mayfield's return While Mayfield is set to return, Tampa has injury concerns elsewhere on its offensive depth chart. WR1 Emeka Egbuka has already been ruled out due to a concussion, and Mayfield will be without starting right tackle Luke Goedeke as well as he battles a calf issue. Still, the Bucs boast a veteran offensive line even wihtout Goedeke in the lineup, and Mayfield should have plenty of opportunity to move the ball against a suspect Panthers defense. His return means good things for Bucky Irving, who went nuts in the prime time win over the Cowboys two weeks ago but has largely faced stacked boxes with Daniels starting. Egbuka's absence certainly hurts, but rookie Ted Hurst becomes a viable FLEX play for fantasy owners after catching six balls for 40 yards last week against the Steelers. Chris Godwin should also see plenty of targets as by far the most experienced target left in this beleaguered receiver room. Losing Baker Mayfield to a thumb injury is far from the only reason the Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently find themselves in the NFC South cellar ; the team was 0-3 with its starting quarterback in the lineup, after all. But, with all due respect to UDFA Jalon Daniels , who has filled in as admirably as could have been expected in Mayfield's absence, it's hard to see Tampa s alvaging anything from this season without Mayfield back under center.
