home.headline: Elijah Arroyo injury update: Seattle Seahawks receive devastating news as young tight end faces another major setback in promising NFL career
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. That’s real draft capital for a tight end. He tore his ACL in September of 2022 at Miami. That injury limited him to only nine games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will miss the rest of the 2026 season, dealing another significant blow to his development after previous injury setbacks. How much more can Elijah Arroyo’s young career take? The Seattle Seahawks tight end is undergoing shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night’s primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It’s a brutal way to lose a season, and it’s even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won’t see him on the field again until 2027. Arroyo’s development takes a hit As a rookie, he played in 13 games and caught 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, but they’re a reasonable foundation for a first-year tight end learning the NFL game. The 2026 season hasn’t gone the way anyone hoped, though. Through six games, Arroyo had just one catch for 17 yards, obviously much less production than his rookie year. Now he won’t get the chance to turn that around. This shoulder injury is going to set him back a good bit. A second-year jump matters for young tight ends, and Arroyo loses most of that year. Losing those reps hurts. Injury history follows Arroyo from Miami to Seattle Now, Arroyo’s injury history isn’t new . It just hasn’t involved his shoulder until now. Most of his problems have been with his knee. The knee issues followed him to the NFL, though. In December 2025, Arroyo suffered a Grade One knee strain. It resulted in the Seahawks placing him on injured reserve, and him missing the rest of the season. This shoulder injury is a different animal for Elijah Arroyo. It’s the longest absence of his pro career by a wide margin. For a player who has already lost chunks of time in college and the NFL, it’s another frustrating hurdle. What it means for the Seahawks’ tight end room I’m not going to pretend this changes everything for Seattle. It’s obvious Arroyo came in to be the No. 2 tight end, even as a fairly high draft pick. The Seahawks are set at the position with AJ Barner leading the way. Seattle’s passing game will keep running through its top options, and the tight end room isn’t suddenly in crisis mode. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Here’s a look at the odds, the latest movement since Sunday night and a quick preview of this primetime matchup. Even with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve and out for the season, Philly has a shot to pull off an upset against a Dallas defense that is 31st in the NFL EPA/Play. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. However, Dallas’ defense remains a bottom three unit in the league, and McKee (215 passing yards in Week 6) was at least able to move the Philly offense. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. Bettors may want to consider the OVER (44.5) with how poor the Dallas defense has been this season. The OVER is 4-2 in Dallas’ six games and 3-3 in the Eagles’ matchup in 2026. He passed for 215 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions in the loss to Carolina, despite missing plenty of pieces on offense. His cupboard won't be as bare in Week 7, with star RB Saquon Barkley expected back. away.headline: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . This article originally appeared on Cowboys Wire: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles likely never saw these circumstances coming. Predicted to battle for the NFC East title, both teams are still in contention, but are hardly the type of outfits that look ready to make any noise come January. Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. Philly snatched him off of Dallas' practice squad last week . Here's a look at the complete injury report from Saturday.

away.headline: How Much Will Seahawks Play Ex-Cowboys All-Pro Amid Injuries?
away.blurb: The 28-year-old has seen limited defensive action this season, but Seattle's injury situation could spur his usage. The versatile safety appeared on Seattle's Friday injury report with a hip injury, earning a questionable designation after participating on a limited basis. Meanwhile, Julian Neal remains on injured reserve with a hamstring issue, while linebackers Drake Thomas and Chazz Surratt have been ruled out. How Much Will Seahawks Play Ex-Cowboys All-Pro Amid Injuries? Unlock the latest Heavy on Seahawks news — direct to your inbox. The Seattle Seahawks are bringing a former All-Pro cornerback back into the fold before Sunday's battle with the Kansas City Chiefs . Seattle officially elevated Trevon Diggs from its practice squad Saturday, Oct. 24, opening up a window for the former Dallas Cowboys standout to contribute. The Seahawks announced the move alongside linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo's elevation and guard Anthony Bradford's activation from injured reserve. But the overarching question is, how much will Seattle actually play Diggs? And his performance through three appearances hasn't been discouraging, even if his playing time was slight. Diggs' Snap Count Could Increase Amid Seahawks Injuries Getty LANDOVER, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 25: Trevon Diggs #7 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on prior to a game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) Diggs has participated in just 21 defensive snaps across three games this season, averaging seven per appearance. His workload has declined in each successive contest: Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers : Nine defensive snaps. Week 5 against the San Francisco 49ers : Eight defensive snaps. Week 6 against the Denver Broncos : Four defensive snaps. Those numbers suggest a restricted role against Kansas City, barring an adjustment to head coach Mike Macdonald's defensive rotation. A reasonable independent projection places Diggs at five to 10 defensive snaps Sunday, with approximately seven as the baseline estimate. However, that outlook could change depending on the availability of Nick Emmanwori . Emmanwori played 58 of Seattle's 60 defensive snaps against Denver, making his potential absence significant. Assuming the second-year defender can't suit up, Diggs' projected workload could rise to approximately 10 to 20 snaps. 15 snaps serves as a reasonable estimate if Seattle shifts Devon Witherspoon into additional slot responsibilities, potentially generating outside opportunities for Diggs or Nehemiah Pritchett . The Seahawks also have Josh Jobe firmly entrenched at cornerback, meaning Diggs could stay as a reserve regardless of Emmanwori's availability. Ex-Cowboys All-Pro Has Allowed One Catch With Seahawks Getty ARLINGTON, TEXAS – DECEMBER 21: Trevon Diggs #7 of the Dallas Cowboys anticipates a play during a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at AT&T Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Arlington, Texas.

away.headline: Recent injury news piles more pressure on Brian Schottenheimer and the Dallas Cowboys ahead of Week 7 matchup versus the Eagles
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Eagles ruled out wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, two of their starters, along with outside linebacker Nolan Smith. If you ask me, that does nothing but raise the pressure on Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer, who has been under heavy scrutiny throughout a 2-4 start. The trenches aren’t in much better shape. Left guard Landon Dickerson is listed as questionable, and he could be activated off injured reserve to play for the first time this season. Meanwhile, right tackle Lane Johnson retired unexpectedly in the middle of the season. Running back Saquon Barkley was a full participant in practice. He’s likely to return from injury, though he has been banged up. And keep in mind, the Eagles were already struggling even when healthy. To be fair, those injuries have been real. All of our evaluations of the Cowboys defense have factored in a banged-up secondary, with multiple injuries at cornerback and safety. Dallas was also without linebacker DeMarvion Overshown for a while-he is set to return on Monday night. Think about the full picture for a second. A backup quarterback, two starting receivers out, their top edge rusher sidelined, a starting tackle retired, and a left guard who hasn’t played all season. That’s the opponent Dallas gets. And if the Cowboys don’t? Honestly, it’s going to be a huge indictment on Schottenheimer and company. There won’t be a banged-up secondary to point to or a missing linebacker to explain things away. The excuses run out when the other sideline is the one dealing with an injury report as extensive as Philly's. The Dallas Cowboys have spent much of their 2-4 start dealing with injuries. This weekend, Philadelphia is the team running thin, and that changes the conversation around the coaching staff. The Dallas Cowboys already knew they would face the Philadelphia Eagles without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. With Tanner McKee under center instead, that alone tilted the matchup in Dallas’ favor. Saturday’s final injury report takes that to the next level. . Just how shorthanded are the Eagles? Start with the offense. Smith and Wicks are two of Philadelphia’s three starting wide receivers, alongside rookie Makai Lemon. Take both of them away, and McKee is left throwing to a rookie and whoever is next on the depth chart. On defense, Nolan Smith leads all Eagles edge rushers in snaps. Losing him removes the most-used piece of their pass rush. The tables have flipped for the Cowboys Here’s the thing about this Cowboys team: injuries have been part of nearly every conversation about them. Whether Dallas meant to or not, it has used them almost as an excuse. This week, the script is reversed. The Cowboys are the ones holding the advantage from an injury standpoint, and the Eagles are the ones patching holes on both sides of the ball. away.headline: 3 things to love about Cowboys-Eagles tilt include playing a pocket QB
away.blurb: For the second time in three weeks, the Cowboys will be playing against a backup quarterback. Hurts is out for the year with blood clots in his lungs, sidelining him until the 2027 season. That transition hasn’t gone well yet. The Eagles have only averaged 2.6 yards a carry in the last three weeks, albeit without Saquon Barkley who should return. In the last two games they’ve rushed for a paltry 57 yards combined, while the offense has converted on just 12 of their last 42 third down attempts. It’s an Eagles team that’s been hurt by players missing time and they’re riding a losing streak twice as long as the Cowboys. That’s not something Brian Schottenheimer’s team will be worrying about on Monday Night Football. Instead, they’ll be trying to bury the Eagles further in the standings. There’s no better satisfaction than beating the Eagles, and here are three reasons to love the Week 7 matchup for the Cowboys. Taking over for Hurts is Tanner McKee, who struggled in his first career start. Against the Carolina Panthers , McKee completed just over 50% of his passes and couldn’t move the offense until the fourth quarter, when the defense was playing soft and allowing completions to keep the clock moving. McKee also gives the Cowboys a break from playing against a mobile QB. Hurts could beat defenses with his legs, something McKee cannot do at nearly the same level, rushing for zero yards last week. Dallas’ defense has a chance to get right against an inexperienced backup QB; that’s a big reason to love the Week 7 matchup. It wasn’t that long ago when the Eagles had what was considered the gold standard in the NFL for the offensive line. A group that was filled with top-tier talent has been reduced to a OL that’s playing with just two of their original starters from the beginning of the season. The sudden retirement of Lane Johnson and the trade of center Cam Jurgens set forth a rebuilding up front. That’s not good and the offensive line is a part of the problem. The Cowboys have a chance to continue to make the transition difficult for the Eagles’ OL. The Eagles have talent on defense, but they aren’t playing up to their potential. Vic Fangio’s unit is allowing over 119 ypg on the ground, and over 244 yards a contest through the air, which is its worst effort since Fangio arrived in 2024. Although the defense has only allowed eight passing scores, the Eagles are also tied for fourth in the league giving eight rushing scores, despite playing against only one, top-10 running back. It’s also a defense that’s known for getting after the quarterback, yet they are tied for next to last in sacks through six games with eight. That’s the same amount as the Cowboys, who have had major problems in generating pressure. After a rough two-week stretch on offense, the Cowboys need to continue to make life miserable on an underperforming defense. It could be the perfect elixir for what ails the Cowboys’ offense. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. Predicted to battle for the NFC East title, both teams are still in contention, but are hardly the type of outfits that look ready to make any noise come January. Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. home.blurb: Saquon Barkley’s return to practice gave the Eagles an encouraging sign Thursday, but another lengthy injury report raised concerns about their passing game ahead of Monday night’s matchup against Dallas. Philadelphia listed 24 players, including six who did not participate. DeVonta Smith sat out with a hamstring injury, Dontayvion Wicks was sidelined with an ankle injury, and Dallas Goedert did not practice because of a knee injury. Barkley was listed as limited with his hamstring injury after missing the past two games. NFL Network reported earlier Thursday that he was expected to practice and was in line to play against Dallas. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards on 36 carries this season, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt. Philadelphia also had eight limited participants, including Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Drew Kendall and Tyler Steen. Dickerson was listed with knee and pectoral injuries, while Hunt was listed with knee and ankle injuries. Michael Carter, Willie Lampkin and Nolan Smith joined the three pass catchers as nonparticipants. Smith remains listed with a concussion after leaving against Carolina. Among the encouraging developments, Jordan Davis practiced fully after leaving Sunday’s game with shin and thumb injuries. Zack Baun, Marquise Brown, Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers also participated fully. Thursday’s report reflects practice participation, not final availability. The Eagles have two more scheduled practice reports before they can determine game designations in their attempt to end a four-game losing streak.
